Atlanta's 56 Marietta Street and adjacent downtown carrier-hotel buildings have long served as major regional telecom interconnection points, and CenturyLink/Lumen's Atlanta presence, inherited through a long chain of legacy mergers (US West, Qwest, Embarq, and others absorbed into what became CenturyLink before the 2020 Lumen rebrand), likely includes both purpose-built colocation space and older central-office infrastructure; no evidence located this session distinguishes which category this specific record falls into. Georgia is one of the 20 states included in Lumens 2022 divestiture of its legacy CenturyLink local telephone operations to Brightspeed, a new company formed by investment firm Apollo Global Management for 7.5 billion dollars plus 1.4 billion dollars in assumed debt in a deal that closed October 3, 2022. If this Atlanta area building remains an active telecom facility, it may now operate under the Brightspeed name rather than CenturyLink, though this registry has not found a source confirming that transfer for this specific building among the six candidate Lumen addresses identified in the metro area and does not assert it.
